strings.Las cuatro frases son del vuelo; la subi: The four sentences are about the flight; the rise in heart rate that two of these studies report is after flight, not during it.
strings.Miden distinto: medidas cortas sentados: They measure differently: short seated measurements (Hughson 2012) versus 24 h ambulatory pressure (Norsk 2015). Baevsky 2007 says «BP», without separating systolic from diastolic.
strings.Miden distinto: en reposo y frente a de: They measure differently: at rest and versus standing before flight, on flights of 9 or 14 days (Prisk 1995), versus missions of 162 to 196 days on the ISS (Baevsky 2007).
strings.Con la misma presión inspirada de oxígen: With the same inspired oxygen pressure (127 mmHg) on Earth and in the Space Shuttle cabin, which breathed 26.5 % oxygen at 527 mmHg; it was not measured in the ISS atmosphere.
strings.La frase es de la estación Mir (5 tripul: The sentence is from the Mir station (5 crew members, Nightcap monitor): sleep shortened with the same sleep opportunity.
strings.Es la estación Mir (5 tripulantes, monit: It is the Mir station (5 crew members, Nightcap monitor); efficiency is the share of the sleep opportunity that was spent asleep.
strings.Solo al principio del vuelo («during ear: Only at the start of the flight («during early flight only»). The sentence is about speed: slower is a longer reaction time. It is the 3-minute PVT of the Cognition battery.
strings.Ningún resumen nombra la SDNN: uno habla: No abstract names SDNN: one speaks of time-domain indicators during sleep; the other, of total spectral power over 24 h.
strings.Ningún resumen nombra la RMSSD: uno habl: No abstract names RMSSD: one speaks of time-domain indicators during sleep; the other two, of the high-frequency band, which falls in Hughson 2012 (6 astronauts) and does not change in Baevsky 2007 (8 cosmonauts, short recordings).
strings.Es la temperatura central, no la de la p: It is core temperature, not skin temperature.
strings.La pérdida es de los primeros 30 días; d: The loss is in the first 30 days; after that, mass was maintained.
strings.Las dos primeras frases hablan de los ma: The first two sentences speak of resorption markers as a whole (on Mir and on the ISS), and N-telopeptide is named in the post-landing sentence of Smith 2005; the third (Zwart 2018, 17 astronauts) names it in flight.
strings.Miden misiones distintas: 6 meses en la: They measure different missions: 6 months on the ISS (Crucian 2015, 23 astronauts: the count rises) versus short Space Shuttle flights (Crucian 2013, 19 astronauts, blood drawn about 24 h before landing: no change).
The abstract does not say which eye.
strings.Frente a sentado antes del vuelo. Tumbad: Versus seated before flight. Supine before flight the area was larger than in flight (80.7 versus 70.3 mm²): the direction depends on the posture it is compared with.
strings.Dos cosmonautas de la Mir en 1993, con l: Two Mir cosmonauts in 1993, with saliva taken in the first 18 days of flight (rises), versus 8 from a long mission on the ISS, on days 90 and 150 (no significant change; out of 12 in the study), and in the discussion Buchheim 2019 gives it as «moderately affected». It may be early versus mid flight: no late measurement rises. Neither of the two sentences says how much or against which sample.
strings.Solo al principio del vuelo; después vol: Only at the start of the flight; afterwards it returned to the earlier values. The abstract warns of the possible influence of dehydration or of plasma volume changes («While susceptible to the possible influence of dehydration or plasma volume alterations»).
strings.En las tres tomas de vuelo; con la misma: At the three in-flight draws; with the same caveat about dehydration or plasma volume that the abstract gives.
strings.Parte de la subida es del retraso de has: Part of the rise comes from the delay of up to 48 h before analysis, which swells the corpuscular volume; the article attributes it to both things («a combination of a true in-flight increase in RBC count and an artifactual increase in MCV resulting from the processing delay»).
Significant only at the end of the flight.
strings.Al principio y a mitad del vuelo; al fin: At the start and in the middle of the flight; at the end it was no longer significantly higher than before («was not significantly higher than pre-flight by the late time point»).
strings.Los resultados lo dan como granulocitos: The results give it as granulocytes («granulocyte levels increased during flight»); the discussion attributes it to neutrophils.
strings.Una sola frase, de porcentajes de frotis: A single sentence, on blood smear percentages on a mission of more than 140 days on the ISS (8 and 10 cosmonauts on flight days 90 and 150); the study warns that in flight it could only look at those percentages.
strings.El resumen no dice si es orina de 24 hor: The abstract does not say whether it is 24-hour urine or what it is compared with.
strings.Una sola frase, de 4 astronautas varones: A single sentence, on 4 male astronauts on a flight the abstract neither names nor says how long it lasted. The same sentence gives testosterone as falling in flight («decreased during flight»).
strings.Una sola frase, de sangre venosa en ayun: A single sentence, on fasting venous blood of ISS astronauts between 2009 and 2018.
strings.En los resultados, desde el día 120 de v: In the results, from flight day 120 to the end of the mission (39 astronauts). On the differences by countermeasure group, the authors add that «all data were within normal ranges, and the magnitude of change would not be considered clinically significant».
strings.en la ISS, Barger 2014 (Lancet Neurol, a: on the ISS, Barger 2014 (Lancet Neurol, actigraphy) gives in-flight sleep (6.09 h) between the two pre-flight periods (5.86 and 6.41 h) and compares each one with the first week after return, not the flight with before; Jones 2022 (Sleep, 24 astronauts, self-reported sleep) attributes the change between phases to longer sleep after return («which was due to longer sleep durations after returning to Earth»).
strings.Jones 2022 (Sleep, 24 astronautas en la: Jones 2022 (Sleep, 24 astronauts on the ISS, 3-minute PVT-B) attributes the change in response speed between phases to the week before launch («driven by slower PVT-B response speed during the week prior to launch»), not to a comparison of the flight with before.

Jones 2022 (Sleep, 24 astronauts on the ISS) says that lapses varied between mission phases («exhibited variability by mission phase») without comparing the flight with before; Dev 2024 (Front Physiol, 25 astronauts on the ISS) counts them inside the PVT accuracy score, with a threshold of 355 ms and not of 500 ms, and does not give their direction in flight; and Tu 2022 (Sci Rep, 24 astronauts on the ISS, PVT-B) predicts response speed and says that lapses tell high performers apart less well («such as the number of lapses or false starts, were less effective in differentiating high performers such as astronauts»), without giving their direction in flight.
strings.Flynn-Evans 2016 (npj Microgravity, 21 a: Flynn-Evans 2016 (npj Microgravity, 21 astronauts on the ISS) gives the estimated temperature minimum outside sleep in 13 % of sleep episodes before flight and in 19 % in flight («on 13% of sleep episodes during preflight and on 19% of sleep episodes during spaceflight»), without comparing them; and it is the frequency of misalignment, not a phase shift in hours. What does give a shift in hours gives it with a sign, and a sign is not a rise or a fall: Gundel 1997 (J Sleep Res, 4 astronauts on Mir) sees the body temperature phase delayed by about 2 h in space compared with the baseline on Earth («The circadian phase of body temperature was found to be delayed by about 2 h in space compared with baseline data»), and EMMA does not declare which sign its phase shift has relative to mission time, so a delay is not read as «rises» or as «falls»; Monk 1998 (J Biol Rhythms, 4 astronauts, Space Shuttle STS-78, 17 days) sees the rhythms in orbit as «very similar in phase and amplitude to those on the ground», on a mission scheduled to disturb rhythms and sleep as little as possible, so it does not say what happens on a normal schedule, and it disagrees with Gundel 1997; and Dijk 2001 (Am J Physiol, 5 astronauts, two Space Shuttle flights of 16 and 10 days) sees the urinary cortisol rhythm misaligned relative to the imposed schedule of less than 24 h («appeared misaligned relative to the imposed non-24-h sleep-wake schedule»), with no hours and no sign.
strings.Baevsky 2007 (J Appl Physiol, 8 cosmonau: Baevsky 2007 (J Appl Physiol, 8 cosmonauts on the ISS) did the orthostatic test only before and after flight («Orthostatic testing was performed pre- and postflight»): in weightlessness there is no standing up. The same holds in what was read later: Fu 2019 (Circulation, 12 astronauts, 6 months of flight) measured 24 h ambulatory pressure before, during and after, but orthostatic tolerance only before and after («no astronaut experienced orthostatic intolerance/hypotension during activities of daily living before or after spaceflight»); Lee 2015 (Aerosp Med Hum Perform, 20 ISS astronauts and 65 Space Shuttle astronauts) did the tilt test ten days before launch, on landing day and three days later, and measures who completes it, not a pressure drop (and from the ISS it gives 6 astronauts on landing day and 15 at three days); and Wood 2019 (npj Microgravity, 8 astronauts on the ISS) did the stand test before and after and, in flight, as a substitute, the release of thigh cuffs after 3 minutes of occlusion, with a drop in mean pressure that did not change compared with before flight («preflight −19 ± 2 mmHg vs. inflight −18 ± 5 mmHg»): it is mean pressure in response to another stimulus, not systolic pressure on standing, and it is not read as a direction.
strings.el estudio leído de la yugular en vuelo: the study read on the jugular vein in flight (Marshall-Goebel 2019, JAMA Netw Open) measured only the left one («only the left IJV was imaged as part of this study»). What was read later gives no sentence that can be read as a direction for the right one: Zamboni 2026 (Sci Rep, 4 astronauts on the ISS, right jugular vein only) has in-flight measurements of only one of them, whose area fell compared with supine before flight («The reduction in ASTRO 0 developed between the first and fifth month in orbit»), with the statistics done only between before and after flight and with the authors' warning that studies with the seated reference saw the area rise on entering weightlessness: a series from one person, with no in-flight statistics and versus supine, is stated and not read as a direction; Arbeille 2015 (Eur J Appl Physiol, 10 astronauts, 6 months) sees the jugular area rise in flight compared with before (JV: 178 and 225 %) without the sentence saying which side (Marshall-Goebel 2019 cites it as the right one examined earlier in flight); Pavela 2022 (Vasc Med, 11 astronauts on the ISS) did duplex ultrasound of both jugular veins in flight and gives peak velocity and echogenicity, not area («none had more than mild echogenicity in the right internal jugular vein»); and David 2021 (Aerosp Med Hum Perform, one astronaut) gives the difference of the right area in flight versus the angles of a tilt table, without its sign.
strings.Mehta 2017 (npj Microgravity, 23 astrona: Mehta 2017 (npj Microgravity, 23 astronauts on the ISS) says that the diurnal trajectory of salivary cortisol changed in flight («The mean diurnal trajectory of salivary cortisol changed significantly during flight»), not that it rises or falls; Agha 2020 (J Appl Physiol, 8 ISS crew members) gives the cortisol/DHEA ratio as elevated before (L-180) and during the mission, not cortisol, and cortisol as higher in those who shed some latent virus than in those who did not; Mehta 2014 (Brain Behav Immun, 17 Space Shuttle astronauts) gives salivary cortisol before and during flight as elevated relative to after («Salivary cortisol measured preflight and during flight were elevated relative to post-flight»), not the flight versus before, and what rises in flight is the cortisol/DHEA ratio.
strings.Trudel 2022 (Nat Med, 14 astronautas en: Trudel 2022 (Nat Med, 14 astronauts on the ISS) gives in flight the products of haemoglobin degradation; haemoglobin itself, one year after landing. Markin 1998 (Acta Astronaut, 17 Mir cosmonauts, fingerstick blood analysed on board) gives it in flight a tendency to fall, without statistics («tendency to decrease of CK activity, hemoglobin»), which is not read as a direction.
strings.Kunz 2017 (BMC Hematol, ISS) ve subir el: Kunz 2017 (BMC Hematol, ISS) sees mean corpuscular volume rise in the in-flight samples, but attributes it to the delay before analysis and not to the flight («we do not identify any MCV variations attributable to spaceflight»); Trudel 2022 (Nat Med, 14 astronauts on the ISS) does not name it in its full text, which gives haemolysis in flight and not the corpuscular indices.
strings.Kunz 2017 (BMC Hematol, ISS) la midió y: Kunz 2017 (BMC Hematol, ISS) measured it and left it out of the analysis as unstable after the delay before analysis («not included in any subsequent analysis due to instability following delayed processing»); Trudel 2022 (Nat Med, 14 astronauts on the ISS) does not name it in its full text, which gives haemolysis in flight and not the corpuscular indices.
strings.Crucian 2015 (npj Microgravity, ISS) da: Crucian 2015 (npj Microgravity, ISS) gives in flight granulocytes rising and lymphocytes unchanged, but not the ratio; Paul 2020 (Front Immunol) reanalyses data from 23 astronauts and gives the granulocyte/lymphocyte ratio as elevated at 180 days of flight («In humans, GLR was elevated at 180-days in-flight»), not the NLR, which it says was not recorded («Retrospective NLR data were not recorded for this mission»): the in-flight NLR is that of the rodents, and the rest of the work is in mice and in cultures; Crucian 2013 (J Clin Immunol, 19 Space Shuttle astronauts) gives the white blood cell differential as unchanged in flight and does not give the ratio either.

Crucian 2015 (npj Microgravity, ISS) gives in flight absolute leukocyte counts, not percentages; Buchheim 2019 (Front Physiol, 12 cosmonauts on the ISS) puts the in-flight neutrophil percentage in its figure 2B («Relative counts (%) of neutrophils lymphocytes and monocytes evidenced by blood smear analysis»), which was not read, and its text only gives the post-flight rise («an increase of neutrophils and monocytes post-flight»); Crucian 2013 (J Clin Immunol, 19 Space Shuttle astronauts) gives the white blood cell differential («differential») as unchanged, without naming neutrophils or saying whether they are counts or percentages, and its abstract does not say which subsets it leaves out of «Most».

Crucian 2015 (npj Microgravity, ISS) gives in flight absolute counts (leukocytes rising and lymphocytes unchanged), not percentages; Crucian 2013 (J Clin Immunol, 19 Space Shuttle astronauts) gives the white blood cell differential («differential») as unchanged, without saying whether they are counts or percentages.
strings.Las dos frases de sin cambio en vuelo so: The two sentences of no change in flight have vitamin D as the intervention, and an analyte that is supplemented is not read as a direction of the flight: Zittermann 2000 (Eur J Clin Invest, one cosmonaut, N = 1, 20 days, with a daily vitamin D2 supplement: «25-hydroxyvitamin D levels did not change significantly») and Heer 2002 (Nutrition, review of European missions: on the 21-day Mir 97 mission, with a vitamin D supplement, «total 25-OH-Vitamin D levels were unchanged», without saying how many astronauts), which appear to be the same mission. Morey-Holton 1988 (Aviat Space Environ Med, 4 Spacelab 2 astronauts, 8 days) gives plasma 25OHD as «essentially normal during the mission», with no direction; Smith 2012 (J Bone Miner Res, 13 ISS crew members) gives a «nominal» vitamin D status before and during flight (75 ± 17 nmol/L), with no direction; Smith 2005 (J Nutr, 11 ISS astronauts) gives it as lower after flight, not during («serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol was decreased after flight»).
strings.Smith 2012 (J Bone Miner Res, 13 tripula: Smith 2012 (J Bone Miner Res, 13 ISS crew members) gives bone alkaline phosphatase, not total, and with a non-significant tendency at the end of the flight («tended to increase during flight toward the end of the mission (p = 0.06)»); Zwart 2018 (Am J Clin Nutr, 17 astronauts) also gives the bone-specific one, higher at the end of the flight («bone-specific alkaline phosphatase (BSAP) was higher toward the end of flight»), not total; nothing of what was read measures total in flight.
strings.Smith 2015 (Bone, ISS) habla del calcio: Smith 2015 (Bone, ISS) speaks of urinary calcium («elevates urinary calcium»), not of blood calcium; Smith 1997 (Clin Chem, Space Shuttle, portable analyser on board) gives ionized calcium, not total, as lower in flight («Ionized calcium was decreased in flight and on landing day») and attributes the in-flight changes to the collection technique («Changes during flight were likely related to sample collection technique»); Morey-Holton 1988 (Aviat Space Environ Med, 4 Spacelab 2 astronauts, 8 days) gives plasma calcium as «essentially normal during the mission», with no direction; Heer 2002 (Nutrition, review of European missions) gives total serum calcium as rising on the 21-day Mir 97 mission («Total serum calcium concentration and urinary calcium excretion significantly increased during this mission»), with a calcium-rich diet and a vitamin D supplement and without saying how many astronauts: calcium was the intervention, and an analyte that is supplemented is not read as a direction of the flight. Without that intervention, there is no sentence on total blood calcium in flight.
strings.el Twins Study (Garrett-Bakelman 2019, S: the Twins Study (Garrett-Bakelman 2019, Science, one astronaut 340 days on the ISS and his twin on Earth) measured it before, during and after flight («a large set of biochemical profiles were measured pre-, in-, and postflight for both subjects») and the text does not give its result; the systematic review by Gimunová 2024 (npj Microgravity, 16 studies) only collects it in studies on Earth («Earth»), none in flight, and its only in-flight study with women is the one on the risk of venous thrombosis with combined oral contraceptives.
strings.la revisión sistemática de Gimunová 2024: the systematic review by Gimunová 2024 (npj Microgravity, 16 studies) only collects it in studies on Earth («Earth»), none in flight; the list of biochemistry that the Twins Study (Garrett-Bakelman 2019, Science, one astronaut 340 days on the ISS and his twin on Earth) measured before, during and after flight does not name it.
strings.la revisión de Strollo 1999 (Adv Space B: the review by Strollo 1999 (Adv Space Biol Med) does not give the direction of LH in flight and warns that its pulsatile secretion makes it hard to have representative values («pulsatility poses a problem for obtaining representative values (e.g., for luteinizing hormone)»); and the communication by Strollo 1997 (J Gravit Physiol, Spacelab) gives the aim in its abstract, with LH as a hypothesis («impaired luteinizing hormone (LH) output with consequent testosterone (T) hyposecretion in men»), and gives no results; its text is not online.
strings.en Skylab (Leach y Rambaut 1974, NTRS, n: on Skylab (Leach and Rambaut 1974, NTRS, nine crew members) it was not measured in the in-flight samples and it rose after flight («These include total protein, carbon dioxide, thyroid stimulating hormone and thyroxine»); on the Space Shuttle (Smith 2011, Aviat Space Environ Med, 224 men and 49 women) it rose on landing day while iodinated water was drunk and stopped doing so when the iodine was removed («postflight TSH was not significantly different from preflight values»), with samples only before and after flight; the list of biochemistry that the Twins Study (Garrett-Bakelman 2019, Science, one astronaut 340 days on the ISS and his twin on Earth) measured before, during and after flight names thyroid hormones («thyroid hormones»), not TSH.
strings.en Skylab (Leach y Rambaut 1974, NTRS) l: on Skylab (Leach and Rambaut 1974, NTRS) thyroxine, which was total thyroxine, was not measured in the in-flight samples and rose after flight; on the Space Shuttle (Smith 2011) total thyroxine and the free T4 index, which is not free T4, rose after flight («elevated in men after flight»), with samples only before and after; the Twins Study (Garrett-Bakelman 2019, Science, one astronaut 340 days on the ISS and his twin on Earth) measured thyroid hormones in flight and the text does not give their result; and the review by Strollo 1999 (Adv Space Biol Med) gives thyroxine as lower in space («which are lowered in space») without saying whether it is the free one or which study it comes from.
strings.el Twins Study (Garrett-Bakelman 2019, S: the Twins Study (Garrett-Bakelman 2019, Science, one astronaut 340 days on the ISS and his twin on Earth) measured it before, during and after flight («protein carbonyls (myeloperoxidase, lp-PLA2, neopterin, and beta-2 microglobulin)») and the text does not give its result; on Inspiration4 (Jones 2024, Nature, four civilians on a three-day flight) the blood taken in flight is dried blood spot («dried blood spot samples collected in-flight») and the text does not name it.
strings.ni la lista de la bioquímica que el Twin: neither the list of biochemistry that the Twins Study (Garrett-Bakelman 2019, Science, one astronaut 340 days on the ISS and his twin on Earth) measured before, during and after flight nor the text of Inspiration4 (Jones 2024, Nature, four civilians on a three-day flight), whose blood taken in flight is dried blood spot («dried blood spot samples collected in-flight»), names it.
strings.Meck 2004 (Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physi: Meck 2004 (Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol, 23 astronauts on short Space Shuttle flights) measured it in plasma before flight and on return, not in flight («We studied 23 astronauts 10 days before launch, on landing day, and 3 days after landing»); the list of biochemistry that the Twins Study (Garrett-Bakelman 2019, Science, one astronaut 340 days on the ISS and his twin on Earth) measured before, during and after flight does not name it.
strings.Markin 1998 (Acta Astronaut, 17 cosmonau: Markin 1998 (Acta Astronaut, 17 Mir cosmonauts, fingerstick blood analysed on board) gives in flight a tendency to rise for GOT, which is AST («had been found tendency to increase, in compare with basal level, GOT, GPT»), without statistics; like the alkaline phosphatase tendency in Smith 2012, it is not read as a direction.

Markin 1998 (Acta Astronaut, 17 Mir cosmonauts, fingerstick blood analysed on board) gives in flight a tendency to rise for GPT, which is ALT («had been found tendency to increase, in compare with basal level, GOT, GPT»), without statistics; like the alkaline phosphatase tendency in Smith 2012, it is not read as a direction.
strings.Lo leído no coincide y nada da un sentid: What was read does not agree and nothing gives a measured direction: Markin 1998 (17 Mir cosmonauts) gives in flight a tendency to rise, without statistics («tendency to increase, in compare with basal level, GOT, GPT, total amylase activity, glucose»); Grigor'ev 1994 (English abstract of an article in Russian, with two authors in common) says that the biochemical status was examined «during long (4-6 months) space flights», but its sentence on what rises («Space flight was found associated with increased peripheral blood levels of glucose») does not say against what or at which sample; and Stroud 2022 (serum NMR of 51 ISS astronauts), which gives not the concentration but the relative abundance of its signal, names it among what falls from 10 days before launch to flight day 15 («mainly by downregulations of glucose, pyruvate, and ethanol in males»), with the authors' caution that the blood metabolome «does not provide substantial insight into metabolic changes occurring throughout flight relative to pre-flight».
strings.Grigor'ev 1994 (resumen en inglés de un: Grigor'ev 1994 (English abstract of an article in Russian; cosmonauts on flights of 4 to 6 months) gives it as rising («Space flight was found associated with increased peripheral blood levels of glucose, cholesterol, triglycerides, urea»), without saying against what or at which sample; Markin 1998 (17 Mir cosmonauts), with two authors in common and the same analyser, measures it on board and finds no definite trend for it («Some definite trends in variations of other determined biochemical parameters had not been found»).

Grigor'ev 1994 (English abstract of an article in Russian; cosmonauts on flights of 4 to 6 months, fingerstick blood) names them among what rises («Space flight was found associated with increased peripheral blood levels of […] total protein»), but the sentence does not say against what or whether it compares in-flight samples with earlier ones.

Grigor'ev 1994 (English abstract of an article in Russian; cosmonauts on flights of 4 to 6 months) names it among what rises («Space flight was found associated with increased peripheral blood levels of […] lactate dehydrogenase»), but the sentence does not say against what or whether it compares in-flight samples with earlier ones; nothing else of what was read names it.
strings.Markin 1998 (Acta Astronaut, 17 cosmonau: Markin 1998 (Acta Astronaut, 17 Mir cosmonauts) measures creatinine in flight and finds no definite trend for it («Some definite trends in variations of other determined biochemical parameters had not been found»); Zheng 2023 (Front Physiol, 27 ISS astronauts) gives it in a table with arrows and not in a sentence: in serum, of the 18 astronauts with a significant trend, the majority one in flight is lower than before, with a secondary one higher; and in the text it places creatinine, without saying in which fluid, in a group of measures with «a gradual increase in intensities».
strings.Nada de lo leído da el cociente: Grigor': Nothing of what was read gives the ratio: Grigor'ev 1994 gives urea as rising, without saying whether it compares in-flight samples with earlier ones, and does not name creatinine; Markin 1998 (Mir) measures both in flight and finds no definite trend for them.
strings.Markin 1998 (Acta Astronaut, 17 cosmonau: Markin 1998 (Acta Astronaut, 17 Mir cosmonauts) measures gamma-GT in flight and finds no definite trend for it («Some definite trends in variations of other determined biochemical parameters had not been found»).

Markin 1998 (Acta Astronaut, 17 Mir cosmonauts) measures total bilirubin in flight and finds no definite trend for it («Some definite trends in variations of other determined biochemical parameters had not been found»).
strings.Markin 1998 (Acta Astronaut, la Mir) mid: Markin 1998 (Acta Astronaut, Mir) measures in flight only total bilirubin («total bilirubin»), with no definite trend; direct bilirubin is not named by anything of what was read.
strings.Zwart 2022 (J Appl Physiol, astronautas: Zwart 2022 (J Appl Physiol, ISS astronauts) gives it as lower after flight, not during («All the astronauts had lower levels of serum albumin after flight than they did before the flight»); of the flight it only counts how many had some low measurement, more among the women astronauts who were taking combined oral contraceptives.
strings.Zheng 2023 (Front Physiol, 27 astronauta: Zheng 2023 (Front Physiol, 27 ISS astronauts) gives sodium, without saying in which fluid, in a table with arrows and not in a sentence: of the 18 astronauts with a significant trend, the majority one in flight is lower than before, with a secondary one higher.

Zheng 2023 (Front Physiol, 27 ISS astronauts) only carries in its table of the most frequent findings (16 astronauts or more with a significant trend) potassium in urine, not in blood; Smith 1997 (Clin Chem, Space Shuttle, portable analyser on board) gives it as rising in flight («Potassium increased in flight compared with before flight») and attributes the in-flight changes to the collection technique («Changes during flight were likely related to sample collection technique»), so it is not read as a direction.
Zheng 2023 (Front Physiol, 27 ISS astronauts) only carries in its table of the most frequent findings (16 astronauts or more with a significant trend) chloride in urine, not in blood.
Zheng 2023 (Front Physiol, 27 ISS astronauts) only carries in its table of the most frequent findings (16 astronauts or more with a significant trend) phosphorus in urine, not in blood.
strings.Zwart 2022 (J Appl Physiol, ISS) da la P: Zwart 2022 (J Appl Physiol, ISS) gives high-sensitivity CRP in a table, with the effect of time «ND» (not different) and differences between groups that the pairwise analysis does not bear out («though no post hoc differences were statistically significant»); Zwart 2013 (Am J Clin Nutr, 23 ISS crew members) says that acute phase proteins show no inflammation in flight («Acute phase proteins indicated no evidence of an inflammatory response during flight») and Lee 2020 (J Appl Physiol, 13 astronauts) that inflammation markers rise in flight («Biomarkers of oxidative stress and inflammation increased during spaceflight»), without either abstract naming CRP; in the Twins Study (Garrett-Bakelman 2019, N = 1) CRP rises after landing, not in flight («CRP levels rose at R+0 and continued to rise at R+4 days»); and on Inspiration4 (Jones 2024, three days) the in-flight CRP test detected nothing on the devices («no IgM or CRP were detected for the devices run in space following standard protocol»), and the authors link it to storage humidity.
